the programme is finished and failed. GSK and iTeos terminated the belrestotug development programme in May 2025 after the Phase 2 GALAXIES Lung-201 interim showed that belrestotug plus dostarlimab gave no clinically meaningful progression-free survival benefit over dostarlimab alone in previously untreated PD-L1-high NSCLC, and enrolment in the Phase 3 GALAXIES Lung-301 (NCT06472076) was halted at 88 participants. Every NSCLC study the dossier lists runs through that decision: NCT06472076 still reads 'Active, not recruiting' in the registry with 88 enrolled (last update 2026-07-21), which is why the book carried it as a live Phase 3; NCT05565378 is GALAXIES Lung-201 itself, whose four substudy arms are all belrestotug-containing (1A, 1B, 1C dostarlimab plus belrestotug, 2A dostarlimab plus belrestotug plus nelistotug); and NCT06405230, the GSK-sponsored biomarker study, is TERMINATED as of 2026-07-13 (ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, read 2026-10-27)

column11: a judgement, and the case for a high one. Nothing is approved for perioperative treatment of dMMR colon cancer, so a positive readout creates the standard rather than competing for it, and the biology has already produced the most striking result in the field: dMMR locally advanced rectal cancer answered to dostarlimab with sustained complete clinical responses, which is the basis of Jemperli's own accelerated approval in that setting. The tumour is biomarker-selected, the patients are identified before surgery by a test that is already standard of care, and the treating centres are the same academic centres that run the rectal protocol. Set against that, a perioperative schedule competes with proceeding straight to surgery, and adoption in a curative setting follows disease-free survival data rather than response rates
